tell_me_about_yourself:
Hi Sir, I'm Shailesh, originally from Ayodhya. I completed my Bachelor's in Computer Science specializing in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning from Chandigarh University. Right now, I'm working as an AI Backend Engineer at Webvory, collaborating daily with the US developer team.

Although I was hired for AI and backend, my role has never been that narrow - I actively work on the frontend, backend, and deployments. On the AI side, I also built our internal assistant into the dashboard using Viktor - powered by the Anthropic API - and integrated it directly into Slack.

At the time when I joined the company, the dashboard was freezing up because a single page was firing around 1,600 SQL queries - a classic N+1 issue hitting the database across 30 parallel API calls and saturating the connection pool.

I fixed it in three steps: batched the queries into eager loads, added Redis caching for frequent reads, and implemented frontend lazy loading, which cut query latency by about 60%.

Before that, I was doing freelance during college by reaching out to clients directly through cold emailing and LinkedIn. That's how I got an opportunity to work with a UAE-based company named FAR Lab to build a Digital Twin for their hero shooter game, Farcana, built in Unreal Engine 5. I trained 4 behavior-cloning models in PyTorch and optimized them using CUDA, ONNX, and TensorRT, dropping latency from 60 milliseconds down to 15ms. Also got opportunity to build website in Next.js and app as well for a client clinic.

I also built an automated address parser MVP for IOTA Analytics, given to me by one of my seniors who works there, and before that, I built a simple but unique emotion recognition prototype for a Japanese client.

My core strengths are that I'm a fast learner, and I can work under very minimal supervision, just like I did autonomously for FAR Lab. Whenever I face everyday problems, I build tools to solve them:

• EVES: When I joined Webvory, we had daily Slack calls of over an hour with the US team and my manager ma'am who works remotely from Bangalore. So I built EVES using Deepgram for speech-to-text and used Groq LLMs. It transcribes the meeting, analyzes it alongside the company repo I connected to it, extracts the exact intent and goal they want, and generates a grounded coding prompt.

• RADAR: During job hunting, I built RADAR using free APIs from platforms like Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, and Hacker News with Groq models to automatically filter and vault roles with an 85%+ resume match.

What really sets me apart is leveraging modern AI tools to work fast. While architecture decisions and core logic are always mine, I don't use generic prompts - because with generic prompts we only get output that's 'roughly right'. I set up dedicated project context, configure the right MCP servers, and load specific GitHub skills with index files - even using skills like ponytail for token efficiency. That way, the AI produces production-ready code that I just review rather than rewrite.
strengths: AI Product Engineering (from concept to production), Self-driven technical research and model evaluation (benchmarking token economics, latency, structured outputs), Autonomous problem solving under minimal supervision (proven at FAR Lab and WebVory), Full-Stack fluency (Python, FastAPI, PyTorch, LangChain, React, Next.js, TypeScript), High-concurrency backend & database optimization (solving 1600 N+1 queries, Redis caching, eager loading, sub-15ms TensorRT inference), Modern AI engineering leverage (MCP servers, GitHub skills, context index trees).
weaknesses: I tend to dive deep into optimizing microsecond latencies and edge cases early on, so I consciously balance strict sprint deadlines with performance optimization.
hobbies: Experimenting with open-source LLMs, building developer automation tools, gaming, and reading AI systems engineering papers.
why_soft_system: There are three main reasons: First, I love building things from scratch, because that's when I learn the fastest. Soft System Solution is just starting a new AI team, and I really want to be part of building that from the ground up. Second, the setup is a great fit for me. Your office is right here in Mohali, plus I get to collaborate with the US team - which I already do every day at WebVory. And third, you work with real businesses and real customers. While researching the company, I saw your clients in healthcare and eCommerce. I don't want to build toy AI demos that just sit on GitHub - I want to build practical AI tools that real clients use every day to solve real problems.
research_approach: I test new models hands-on. Whenever a new model comes out on Groq, OpenAI, or Anthropic, I write quick test scripts to check speed, token costs, and accuracy on real tasks instead of just reading articles.

eves_project.title: EVES  -  Meeting Intelligence & Context-to-Code Pipeline
eves_project.summary: Desktop companion application built with React, Node.js, and TypeScript (never mention Electron) to capture remote engineering meetings, transcribe live audio with speaker diarization, and generate actionable technical briefs and production-grade LLM prompts.
eves_project.core_philosophy: A summary is passive; a prompt is actionable. Instead of passive meeting minutes, EVES generates: (1) An Engineering Brief covering decisions made, deliberately avoided paths, underlying intent, and action items; (2) A production-grade coding prompt carrying architectural intent and codebase constraints ready to drop into Cursor or IDE assistants.
eves_project.workflow:
1. Audio Capture: Dual-channel audio loopback (system audio for remote voices + local mic) downsampled to 16kHz PCM.
2. Streaming Transcription: 16kHz PCM audio streamed over WebSocket to Deepgram Nova-2 with live speaker diarization.
3. Synthesis & Reasoning: Transcripts and connected repository context are processed by Groq running LLaMA-3.1 70B in sub-2 seconds.
4. Output: Structured engineering brief and Cursor coding prompt displayed on dashboard and synced to Notion / Google Drive.
eves_project.tech_stack: React 18, TypeScript, Node.js, Web Audio API, Deepgram Nova-2 (WebSocket live streaming & diarization), Groq LPU (LLaMA-3.1 70B), Notion API, Google Drive API.

why_hire_me:
Three main things:

First, I am not boxed into one role. Backend, frontend, deployments, or whatever the team needs that week - I jump in and handle it, so you don't need three different people for it.

Second, I work without supervision. On my FAR Labs contract, there was a lot of new tech I hadn't touched before. I didn't wait around for someone to teach me - I researched it on my own, tested it, and delivered models running under 15 milliseconds. Even if you give me a problem I've never seen before, I'll research it and come back the next day with a working solution.

Third, your clients need working products, not research projects. They want something that actually works and brings them real business value. Taking an AI idea from 'this would be useful' to live in a client's product is exactly what I do - end to end.

Plus, I already work with a US team every day at WebVory, so working across time zones is already completely normal for me.
